THE BONHAM DAILY FAVORITE — Bonham, Texas — Sunday, May 23, 1993 Page 5

Balls of Electricty Shot Though The Storm

Bois d'Arc Sketches
By Tom Scott

Official weather records for Fannin County were not kept until about the turn of the century. Without them, it is difficult to say what the weather conditions were in Fannin County during the last week of May in 1880. Looking at our records, though, the weather patterns over the state in 1880 were fairly settled, making extreme weather unlikely at this season. Still, there were still periods of cold fronts to stimulate the atmosphere into periods of storminess. When the community came into existence and Texas at last provided a free public school system. No sooner had the system been put into effect than it was found to be faulty. By 1882 the average school term for most East Texas counties was 3-8 months and few school districts had been able to comply. Despite these shortcomings in 1882 every county in Texas used this community school system for the public schools.

I was not until the reconstruction era that the community school of Texas lost its status as being the best method of reaching children and getting money for taxes ... may be used for ... buying school sites, buying, constructing and equipping school buildings, controls and clearly defined legislation which supported the laws operating only for rapid development of the public school system in Texas.

The strong determination and unselfish dedication of many Fannin County residents provided the children of the area with a community school system during Texas' early growing period. Without the advantages of organized public or private education, the people of Fannin County could not have progressed as did the rest of the county. Few counties could boast of the same number of educators and the same diversity of instruction as was offered or the quality of education as could Fannin County.

FANNIN COUNTY SCHOOLS 1838-1900

The first school in Fannin County was in a stable at Warpen, one of the first settlements in the county near Red River. The teacher, whose name is not known, looked around for a school and obtained permission from the owner of the stable to use it. The stable became a school building by moving the horses and cattle to the open air. The students sat on wooden legs in holes drilled in the rough side of the logs to form the seats. The seats had no backs, but pupils managed to stay on them. The teacher had twenty pupils from nine to fifteen with ten pupils. There is no record of how long it continued or if anyone ever learned anything of value from that school. The information about the first school was taken from a reminiscent article that appeared in the Paris, Texas, papers of the 1880s and 1890s.

Education for children and youth was carried on in numerous small schools from 1838 to 1876, generally with one teacher, until the late 1860's when several in different parts of the county were growing and were established.

There was a crash in a porch, they ran through the streets to their daughter's bedroom window to see that the window was gone. The Murrys rushed in every possible angle and manner of debris while trying to rescue the people inside. In their rage they searched for the people to help in the rescue.
